principles: Preserve porcelain rows byte-exactly from git to parser; only per-line trailing-whitespace normalization is allowed
Fix at the read site with the already-reviewed B-b264 raw-read pattern, never via a cross-cutting refactor in gate-adjacent code
Every affected consumer gets a first-row modified-tracked regression assertion that fails on the pre-fix code
Untouched call sites carry a recorded audit verdict so the no-change decision is itself reviewable
drivers: First-row corruption reaches material/volatile classification in DONE-gate evidence snapshots, review preflights and recovery guards
Untracked-only fixtures systematically miss the class, so regression tests must stage tracked-modified first rows and assert row shape
Minimize diff and review risk: the affected files feed high-assurance gates

options.name: per-site raw-read fix (B-b264 pattern)
pros: bounded diff over exactly the six affected sites
matches the pattern reviewers already accepted in B-b264
shared helpers serving non-porcelain callers stay untouched
cons: future consumers can still copy a full-trim helper (mitigated by the audit table + regression smoke)

options.name: shared git-status module refactor
pros: single choke point structurally prevents recurrence
cons: large review surface in gate-adjacent code
higher merge risk against concurrent stories

options.name: parser-side shift tolerance (worktree.ts line[2] heuristic everywhere)
cons: keeps corrupted status codes (only paths recovered)
heuristic parsing hides the defect instead of fixing it
every parser needs the tolerance forever

rationale: The user explicitly requested the B-b264 gitRaw/gitStatusRows pattern; it keeps the diff bounded to the six affected consumers in gate-adjacent code, and the recorded audit table plus the first-row regression smoke mitigate the recurrence risk that a shared-module refactor would otherwise address.

preMortem.scenario: regression smoke fixture first row is not the intended modified-tracked row
preMortem.trigger: porcelain row ordering differs across git versions or fixture path names sort differently
preMortem.consequence: regression assertions pass vacuously and the bug class can silently return
preMortem.mitigation: every scenario asserts row 0 matches /^ M / before asserting classification, and fixture paths are chosen to sort deterministically first

preMortem.scenario: new test-only exports break surface contracts
preMortem.trigger: exporting assertMaterialCleanForReview / gitPorcelainPaths / readGitStatus trips cli-surface-smoke or command-catalog-smoke
preMortem.mitigation: exports are plain functions (no CLI commands); run full run-all-smokes before REVIEW

preMortem.scenario: emptiness semantics drift after removing full trim
preMortem.trigger: clean-tree raw output truthiness differs from trimmed output (e.g. trailing newline)
preMortem.consequence: a clean tree is treated as dirty (or vice versa) in evidence snapshots or preflights
preMortem.mitigation: all emptiness decisions move to rows.length===0 after per-line trimEnd + filter(Boolean), never raw-string truthiness

preMortem.trigger: fix mis-scopes the .lattice/ exclusion while converting the read
preMortem.consequence: a materially dirty tree passes the review preflight and binds a dishonest hash (unsound)
preMortem.mitigation: adversarial smoke asserts a material modified-tracked row still throws naming the exact path
